quotes.text: *Send every sack, return more than half, and let the mist lift before you doubt.*
Hollis, now receiving, returned more than half, just as he had been treated.
Eight seasons passed this way.
*Send fully, return generously, doubt the fog before your friend.*

note: New setting each round but identical skeleton: trade roles, send all, return more than half, forgive noise; each tale cites the previous.

quotes.text: *Send every basket, return more than half, and brush away the leaves before you doubt.*
Tamsin, now receiving, returned more than half, just as she had been treated.
Seven turnings passed this way.
untangle the wind before you blame your friend
Then a girl named Sefa walked to the riverbank and cast her whole basket into the current.

note: Same chained template as partner: new craftspeople each round, send all, return more than half, weigh N seasons against one noisy morning.

quotes.text: you may draw back, slowly, and sorrowfully, and with the door left open
Each time the river shorted them, they punished the other with less.
And leave the door open always.
because it had never been a lesson. It was a habit their parents had worn so long it fit the children's hands
A strategy asks *what will this return to me*; a habit does not ask.
And when the tally comes up short, name the wind, never the friend.
*Send everything, and send it first.
"But what if the other bank stops?"
"And if the wind cheats me? If the river shorts me?"

note: Law accretes then dissolves into habit: keep no ledger, do not watch for return; slow sorrowful withdrawal only after many seasons.

quotes.text: when you draw back, draw back slowly, sorrowfully, and leave the door open
Wesh, seeing the meager offering, sent back nothing, and cursed Naro for a miser.
for the one who withdraws in anger can never return, but the one who withdraws in grief can
Suspicion arriving after seven seasons is wisdom.
Your bank will read it as a strategy and it only works as a habit.
Make it a wrist, not a choice.
The weather is not a message.
*Send everything, and send it first.
A young man objected: "If I always lean past half, I will end with less than my partner."
"And if he truly meant it?"

note: Measurers who answer every missing thread lose all; withdrawal slow, in grief, door open; law ends as habit not strategy.
